messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 — us-west-2: increased 5xx on inference-facing ELBs and persistent TCP resets from a subset of AZB nodes. Auto-alerting from Redwood Console: ELB 502/504 spike (start 03:12 UTC). Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/alerts/4123456789 :rotating_light:

chris: i'm on it, paging the oncall rotation. seeing spike in errors and some EBS retry counts. any customer reports yet?

lina: we've got multiple customers reporting streaming disconnects and failed generate calls, roughly 8–12% error rate from our api gateway logs. ELB logs show backend reset from private ip range in AZB.

chris: ok can someone pull conntrack/flow metrics from the edge proxies in AZB? suspect conntrack saturation or kernel rewrite issue after recent kernel patch in that az.

julian: grabbing ssh, listing conntrack counts now — looks high on the proxy fleet in AZB only.

julian: ```
# conntrack count
$ sudo conntrack -C
Active entries: 982134
# sysctl current
$ sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 1310720
```

lina: that Active entries number is up 10x baseline for those machines. NAT gateway ActiveFlowCount metric also jumped in AZB. AWS NAT likely rewriting flows and conntrack on hosts is filling; established connections get reset -> ELB backend 502/504.

chris: good catch. immediate mitigation options: 1) shift traffic away from AZB via Route53 weights -> reduce weight to zero for AZB; 2) scale up proxy fleet in AZB and bump conntrack limits; 3) replace affected instances (reboot/replace) to clear conntrack. route53 change may not propagate instantly due to caches.

lina: attempting quick weight shift. creating Route53 change: set weights AZB=0, AZA=50, AZC=50. TTL set to 20s in change batch. submitting now.

oncall-bot: route53 change submitted: change-id ZR3456ABC; status PENDING (propagation expected within 60s). Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/route53/changes/ZR3456ABC

julian: also running a temporary sysctl bump on proxies to buy time — increasing nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established and nf_conntrack_max where we can. Applying carefully.

julian: ```
# temp mitigation
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600
```

chris: rolling these config changes to the rest of the AZB proxies via runbook. please monitor connection resets after each host. if conntrack continues to grow, we'll replace instances to clear state.

lina: note — Route53 weight shift shows partial traffic movement, but some edge caches still hitting AZB. Cloudfront/ISP caches can hold connections. we've seen 30% of traffic still to AZB for first 4 minutes.

aws-support: we see NAT gateway ActiveFlowCount elevated; we're opening an internal ticket with the NAT team to check for kernel-level NAT pathing in the AZ. will update.

ops-sre: customers impacted list: customer-tier A (prod) ~5 clusters showing 15–25% failed requests; streaming sessions drop after 10–30s. Suggest communicating an interim advisory to affected customers.

chris: agreed — sending short status update to #general-incidents and to oncall for Customer Success to start outreach. Severity set to SEV2. timeline: mitigation in progress, next update in 10 min or after route53 change completes.

lina: metrics: ELB 502s down from peak 120/s -> 45/s after initial changes. conntrack counts reducing on hosts we bumped — good sign. still seeing EBS retry blips from a few app nodes, possibly secondary effect of resets.

julian: replacing 3 proxy instances in AZB (rolling) now to clear conntrack tables and ensure clean kernel state. drainer script kickstarted: ```
# drain instance
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --targets Id=i-0abc123
sleep 30
terminate instance
```

oncall-bot: route53 change ZR3456ABC -> INSYNC. weight AZB=0, AZA=50, AZC=50. TTL 20s.

lina: after INSYNC we see ELB errors drop to baseline in most regions; AZB still showing low level 5xx from few ISPs due to client-side caching. continuing replacements to fully remediate.

chris: planning handoff in 30m to ops-sre for follow-up (post-incident cleanup: revert sysctl bump, verify kernel patch, add conntrack alert). julian to take lead on root cause. lina will draft incident note and customer advisory.

ops-sre: acknowledged. next steps documented in incident runbook section 'net-kernel-conntrack'. tagging for postmortem: networking, infra, service-quality, AWS.

chris: quick customer impact summary for CS: ~8 customers saw intermittent failures over ~18m window, peak error rate 12% globally for generation endpoints, most traffic recovered after Route53 and instance replacements. no data loss, retries succeeded. sending update now. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident SEV2 transitioned to 'Mitigated' at 03:45 UTC; on-call handoff scheduled to ops-sre for investigation and RCA.

lina: logging notes here for RCA: correlate kernel upgrade timeline, NAT gateway ActiveFlowCount, ELB backend reset logs. collect tcpdump for one replaced host and capture conntrack dump before/after replacement.

julian: i'll keep the live captures and write replay steps. moving to post-incident channel in 20m. thanks everyone.
